# Analysis

[id 184]: The passage explicitly distinguishes scaffolding from project-based learning, stating "scaffolding goes a step beyond" project-based learning. Options A, B, and D are all directly supported by the passage. Option C incorrectly equates the two concepts.

[id 185]: The passage specifically states "It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired." This customization feature directly addresses reading difficulties.

[id 186]: The passage states Alexander offered to pay for rebuilding but "his offer was denied," and the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE after "Alexander died." This means it was rebuilt after his reign, not during it.

[id 187]: The passage states Homo Erectus "began walking upright" regularly, while Australopithecus "did not walk upright as habitually," and Sahelanthropus "may have" walked upright—only Homo Erectus is described as regularly walking on two feet.

[id 188]: The passage implies the Allies succeeded because it states Germany would have conquered Britain "had the Allies failed." Since Germany didn't conquer Britain, the Allies (British and Americans) must have had the most naval success.

[id 189]: The passage explicitly states "an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter," making it specifically meant for priests.

[id 190]: The passage explicitly lists foods NOT available to ancient Romans, including turkey, which came from America in later centuries.

[id 191]: The passage states "Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them." Electrons were removed.
